== amd64 DRAP problem

gcc on amd64 (and on i386, but we ignore legacy cases for now)
produces DRAP ("dynamic realign argument pointer") code when a
function needs its stack realigned and also does something that
needs its incoming stack pointer later: alloca/VLAs, outgoing
arguments on the stack (including structs passed by value), nonlocal
gotos, `__builtin_setjmp`/`longjmp` and so on. `-mforce-drap` forces
it. Realignment itself got much more common with x86-64-v3 builds
(e.g. Ubuntu's amd64v3 variant), where spilling AVX values needs a
32-byte aligned stack. See tests/drap/minimal.c and tests/drap/minimal.s.

A DRAP prologue looks like this:

----
  leaq   8(%rsp), %r10     .cfi_def_cfa r10, 0     # DRAP register = CFA
  andq   $-4096, %rsp
  pushq  -8(%r10)                                  # copy of return address
  pushq  %rbp
  movq   %rsp, %rbp        DW_CFA_expression rbp: (DW_OP_breg6 0)
  pushq  %r12                                      # 0+ callee-saved regs
  pushq  %r10              DW_CFA_def_cfa_expression: (DW_OP_breg6 -16; DW_OP_deref)
  pushq  %rbx                                      # more callee-saved regs
----

So the CFA and %rbp are described with DWARF expressions. How many
registers sit between the saved %rbp and the saved DRAP register (and
so the offset in the CFA expression), which register is the DRAP one
(%r10, or %r13 in nested functions, `no_caller_saved_registers`
functions and functions with tail calls, in which case %r13 itself is
pushed first and the CFA is briefly rsp+16), and in which order the
CFI appears all vary. Callee-saved registers, and with
`no_caller_saved_registers` every other register too, get
`DW_CFA_expression` rules of their own.

=== How we handle it

Like gas when it generates SFrame from the same CFI, we don't match
whole prologues. The regular CFI decoder (backtrace-core.cc)
interprets the two expression shapes DRAP uses, both relative to the
frame pointer, for any offset:

* `DW_CFA_def_cfa_expression: DW_OP_breg6 off; DW_OP_deref` is
  `CfaRule::DerefFpRel(off)`: CFA = *(rbp + off).
* `DW_CFA_expression rbp: DW_OP_breg6 off` is
  `RegisterRule::MemFpRel(off)`: caller's rbp is at *(rbp + off).

Everything else in a DRAP FDE is already ordinary: `def_cfa` with
%r10/%r13 is `CfaRule::RegRel`, which needs a register file and so is
only usable in leaf frames, which is fine, because those rows are only
in the prologue and epilogue. Expressions and restores for
non-critical registers are ignored. Any other expression on rbp, rsp
or rip still fails the frame (kFailExpression).

=== gcc's missing .cfi_restore

When the stack is realigned to 64 bytes or less, which covers the
common AVX case of 32 bytes, the epilogue lacks `.cfi_restore 6` after
the `pop %rbp`/`leave`. gcc 10 through 16 all behave this way; with
128 bytes or more they emit the restore. This is
https://gcc.gnu.org/bugzilla/show_bug.cgi?id=128270[gcc bug 128270]:

----
  movq   -8(%rbp), %r10    .cfi_def_cfa r10, 0
  leave                                            # no .cfi_restore 6
  leaq   -8(%r10), %rsp    .cfi_def_cfa rsp, 8
  ret
----

So from the leave on, the CFI says the caller's %rbp is at
*(%rbp + 0) while %rbp already holds the caller's value.
`FixupStaleDRAPEpilogue` in aw-backtrace.cc corrects the two affected
rows (leaf frames only, as no call returns there): right before the
lea that rebuilds %rsp from the DRAP register (recognized by its
bytes), and after it, where an %rsp-based CFA paired with an
fp-relative %rbp rule can only be this stale tail.

=== Tests

tests/amd64-drap-test.cc runs all of these through `drap_test_trampoline`
(an RSP-framed caller, so that getting only RSP wrong is still caught)
and checks that a backtrace from the callee reaches the trampoline:

* `minimal_drap` (tests/drap/minimal.s, realigned to 4096, so with
  `.cfi_restore 6`) and `minimal_drap_2` (the same without it, as gcc
  emits for 64 bytes or less): the classic shape.
* `drap_saved_regs` (tests/drap/regs.s): callee-saved registers
  around the saved %r10, so the CFA expression is breg6 -16.
* tests/drap/variants.s: `drap_many_regs` (breg6 -40) and %r13
  as the DRAP register in `drap_r13_nested` and `drap_r13_ncsr`.

Under the stepped configuration the comparer also checks every
instruction of them, including the prologue and epilogue rows.
